- The white patches are diffuse and appear superficial on the upper leaf surface
- Multiple leaves affected with similar white dusty appearance

This is textbook **Powdery Mildew** (*Blumeria graminis* f. sp. *tritici*) — the white superficial mycelial growth covering the leaf surface is the defining hallmark. No other wheat disease produces this kind of white powdery coating on green leaves. Other candidates like Stripe Rust or Leaf Rust produce orange/yellow pustules; Septoria causes brown lesions; Bacterial Streak causes water-soaked to brown streaks — none match this white powdery appearance.
